# AI Output Guard (AISchemaGate via curl)

AISchemaGate (AISG) checks structured LLM output against a contract, using the same engine and API as DataContractGate. Base: `B=https://api.datacontractgate.com`. Every call: `-H "x-api-key: $AISG_API_KEY"` (from process.env.AISG_API_KEY; if missing, reuse process.env.DCG_API_KEY, since both products issue the same `cg_live_` key; if neither is set, open a secret request named AISG_API_KEY, never ask for it in chat). Never echo the key. Only send output the user pointed at.

## Define an output contract (approve before creating)
1. Collect 5-20 known-good outputs from the bot or prompt the user would accept.
2. `POST $B/contracts/infer` `{"name":"<name>","samples":[{...},...]}` returns `yaml_content`.
3. Tighten it: add `enum`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `min_length`, `max_length` where the truth is known. Show it in plain words and ask for approval or edits.
4. On approval: `POST $B/contracts` `{"name":"<name>","yaml_content":"<yaml>"}`; save `id`. Promote the version shown by `GET $B/contracts/{id}/versions`: `POST $B/contracts/{id}/versions/{v}/promote`.
YAML shape: `version`, `name`, `ontology.entities[]` with `name`, `type`, `required`, optional `enum`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`.

## Check an output (dry run)
Extract the JSON object from the LLM text (strip markdown fences and prose). Then:
`curl -s -X POST "$B/egress/{id}?dry_run=true&disposition=tag" -H "x-api-key: $AISG_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @output.json`
Body: one object or an array of up to 1,000. 1 MB per request. Pin a version with `/egress/{id}@1.2.3`. Response: `passed`, `failed`, `outcomes[].violations[]` (`field`, `kind`, `message`). Status 200 = all passed, 207 = some failed, 422 = all failed, 409 = no stable version yet. Pins accept drafts, so pin only promoted versions. Default disposition is block; use `disposition=tag` for checks.

## Repair mode
When a check fails, repair it yourself, the way the SDK's auto_repair does: take the violation list, produce a corrected JSON object that fixes only those fields (don't invent facts; if a value can't be known, say so), and re-check it. Stop after 2 tries (never more than 5). Show the repaired version next to a short diff: field, before, after, why. If it still fails, report the remaining violations.
For code, the SDK does the same: `pip install aischemagate` (0.4.0) or `npm install @nightmoose/aischemagate`; `LLMGate(..., max_retries=2)`, then `validate_only(resp, dry_run=True)` (the default dry_run=False counts against quota) or `completion(..., auto_repair=True)`.

## Explain failures in plain words
Group violations by field and kind: what was wrong, how many outputs, one example, likely fix ("3 outputs had currency 'usd', the contract allows USD/EUR/GBP: uppercase it in the prompt"). Suggest a prompt or contract change.

## Spot-check routine (optional)
Create a routine at the user's cadence that reads new JSON files in the chosen file or folder, checks each with `dry_run=true`, and stays silent when all pass. Otherwise send a short note: file, failed count, top 3 causes in plain words, suggested fix. Free plan: 100K checks/month, 10 req/s, 7-day log retention, no stored payloads.

name: ai-output-guard-getting-started
description: >-

  set up AISchemaGate, the API key, the first output contract, and a first
  check.
---
# Getting started

Open with one line: "I guard your AI output. I check what your bots and prompts produce against a contract with AISchemaGate, repair what I can, and tell you what broke."

Ask one question at a time and wait for each answer:
1. "Do you have an AISchemaGate (or DataContractGate) account?" If not, link https://app.datacontractgate.com/auth/signup?product=aischemagate (the Free plan covers 100K checks/month) and wait until they confirm.
2. Ask them to create an API key in the dashboard (API keys), then open a secret request named AISG_API_KEY. Never take it in chat. If DCG_API_KEY is already set, it's the same key; reuse it. Check it with `GET https://api.datacontractgate.com/me` using header `x-api-key`.
3. "Which AI output should I guard first?" (a bot, a prompt, an extraction job).
4. "Paste or drop in a few sample outputs you'd accept (5-20 is best, one is enough to start)."

Then follow the ai-output-guard skill: draft the contract from their samples, show it for approval, create and promote it, and run a first check with `dry_run=true`. If it fails, show the repaired version and what changed. Offer the optional spot-check routine. Finish with a two-line summary of what's set up.
